title: JWT in 60 seconds
caption: JWT in 60 seconds: the signed token behind many logins, and what that signature does and does not protect.

scenes.say: After you log in, the server needs to know it's you on every request. A JWT lets it check without looking anything up.
A JWT is three parts: a header, a payload with claims like who you are and when it expires, and a signature.
The signature is the whole point.

items.title: Signed
items.say: The server signs the token with a secret key.

items.title: Tamper-evident
items.say: Change a single character, and the signature no longer matches.

items.title: Readable
items.say: But anyone can read it, so never put secrets in the payload.

scenes.say: That's a JWT. Signed, not secret.
